chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunnān from his father from Ibn al-Mughīrah from al-Sakūnī from Jaʿfar from his father from ʿAlī (peace be upon him) who said:
The black dog's game is not to be eaten, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered its killing.

key_terms.صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: Why is the meat of the black dog not considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the impermissibility of consuming the meat of the black dog, linking the ruling directly to the Prophet’s specific command to kill it. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a sign of its distinct impurity or specific status among animals, distinguishing it from other dogs whose meat might be permissible if slaughtered correctly. The chain of transmission highlights the continuity of this ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq back to Imam Ali, underscoring its foundational nature in fiqh.
